deel.positioning: Owned-entity EOR and contractor payroll in 150+ countries. Deel is the local legal employer.
deel.text_compliance: Deel handles compliance in 150+ countries using a vast network of fully-owned local entities and in-house legal experts. They automate misclassification protection, localized contract generation, tax withholdings, and statutory benefits compliance, backing their contracts with misclassification insurance guarantees.
deel.text_global_reach: Deel provides unmatched international coverage across 150+ countries with direct payroll and owned EOR entities in key tech and hiring hubs globally. They support multi-currency payouts, localized benefits administration, and fast local onboarding.
deel.text_pricing_truth: The $49/contractor and $599/employee figures are platform fees only. Deel Shield, equipment shipping, and background checks are separate SKUs. FX conversion spread hits every fiat payout corridor. Some markets also require a security deposit or payroll prefund (often ~1 month of salary).
choose_if: You will hire full-time staff in several countries this year and Deel issues the local employment contract.
Contractors need USDC or local-currency wallets on the same worker file as employees.

ip_assignment.summary: Deel's owned-entity network means the employment contract that assigns IP is issued by a Deel entity in the worker's own country and then assigned onward to your company. Because the chain runs inside a single corporate group rather than through a partner agency, there is one fewer counterparty sitting between your business and the work product.
bullets: Local employment agreements carry country-specific invention assignment clauses drafted by Deel's in-house legal team rather than one global template.

Civil-law jurisdictions across continental Europe, Japan, and China limit blanket assignment of future inventions, so enforceability depends on local statute rather than contract wording. Ask which of your markets require a separate inventor compensation mechanism.
Contractor agreements handle IP on a different legal footing than EOR employment agreements. Confirm which vehicle each hire sits under before assuming uniform protection.
Deel Shield misclassification cover is indirectly an IP control: a contractor later reclassified as an employee can weaken the original assignment.

tax_withholding.summary: As the legal employer, Deel calculates and remits employer-side contributions, employee income tax withholding, and social security in each market it operates, filing under its own local registrations rather than yours.
bullets: Employer contributions are quoted on top of gross salary and vary widely by country, so budget well above the $599/month platform fee in high-contribution markets.
Statutory 13th-month pay in Brazil, Mexico, Portugal, and the Philippines, and 14th-month pay in Italy, is accrued into monthly employment cost rather than landing as a year-end surprise.
Income tax is withheld at local rates and filed on the local calendar, so finance sees one consolidated invoice instead of managing per-country filings.
Contractor payments carry no withholding at all. Tax responsibility sits with the contractor, which is exactly the exposure Deel Shield is sold to cover.

statutory_benefits.summary: Deel administers the statutory minimum package in each country, covering pension or provident fund, state health insurance, and mandatory leave, with supplemental plans available where local market norms demand more than the legal floor.
bullets: Mandatory PTO floors differ sharply: 30 calendar days in Brazil, 20 days plus public holidays across most of the EU, and no federal minimum in the US. Deel enforces the local floor rather than your global policy.
Severance and notice periods follow local statute, and as legal employer Deel calculates the entitlement and runs the termination process.
Unlawful termination liability sits with the Deel entity rather than your company, which is the core reason an SMB uses an EOR instead of registering a foreign branch.
Supplemental benefits such as private health cover and equity administration are priced separately. Confirm what is bundled in your quote.

fee_structure.summary: The $599/month per employee EOR rate and $49/month per contractor rate are platform fees only. Real total cost of ownership adds employer taxes, FX spread, and per-product add-ons on top.
bullets: FX conversion spread applies on every payout corridor and never appears in the headline rate. Model your actual currencies rather than a USD equivalent.
Deel Shield, equipment procurement and shipping, and background checks are each billed as separate line items.
Some markets require a security deposit or payroll prefunding, commonly framed as a month of salary. Treat this as a working-capital commitment rather than a fee.
Get offboarding and contract-termination terms in writing, since notice-period payroll continues to bill throughout the wind-down.

deel.supportSLA: 24/7 Live Chat, Dedicated CSM, Knowledge Base
deel.skip_if: Don't buy Deel if your team is still US W-2 and you wanted laptops plus payroll on day one. You will fund country coverage you are not using.

gusto.positioning: US payroll, tax filings, and benefits for companies whose people actually sit in the United States.
gusto.text_compliance: Gusto automates local, state, and federal US payroll taxes, including automated filings for 940/941 forms, W-2s, and 1099s. They ensure automated compliance with state-specific overtime laws, workers' compensation requirements, and ACA reporting for domestic teams.
gusto.text_global_reach: Gusto is built primarily for US domestic hiring across all 50 states. While they offer international contractor payments to 120+ countries, they do not provide direct global EOR services for full-time international employees without third-party integrations.
gusto.text_pricing_truth: Published Simple-plan pricing starts at $49/month plus $6/user/month, with higher tiers adding benefits and HR features. International contractor payments carry separate per-transfer costs; confirm FX conversion fees on your payout corridors.
choose_if: Your roster is US W-2 across multiple states and you want federal, state, and local filings without a payroll clerk.
You pay a few overseas contractors. You do not need a foreign employer of record.

ip_assignment.summary: Gusto is a US domestic payroll and HR platform rather than a global Employer of Record. It does not become the employing entity abroad, so it provides no cross-border IP assignment mechanism.
bullets: For US W-2 employees, IP assignment lives in your own employment agreements. Gusto is the payroll system, not the employer.
International contractor payments to 120+ countries carry no EOR-grade assignment. The contract is directly between you and the contractor.
Teams hiring full-time staff abroad need a separate EOR or third-party integration running alongside Gusto.
If protecting R&D output across borders is the priority, this is the wrong layer of the stack for that specific job.

tax_withholding.summary: Gusto's strength is depth in US payroll tax rather than breadth across jurisdictions, with automated federal, state, and local filings including 940/941 forms, W-2s, and 1099s.
bullets: Automated filings cover all 50 states, including state-specific overtime rules and workers' compensation requirements.
There is no employer-side withholding for international contractors. That responsibility sits with the contractor in their own jurisdiction.
13th-month salary has no US equivalent and does not apply to Gusto's domestic model.
International payments carry separate per-transfer costs, so confirm FX conversion fees on your specific corridors.

statutory_benefits.summary: Gusto administers US statutory and voluntary benefits including ACA reporting, workers' compensation, and 401(k), but does not administer foreign statutory benefits anywhere.
bullets: ACA reporting and workers' compensation are handled natively for US teams.
US employment is largely at-will with no federal statutory PTO or severance minimum, a fundamentally different model from EU or LATAM markets.
Gusto provides no unlawful-termination liability shield abroad, because it never becomes the employer.
Companies with even a handful of foreign full-time hires typically run Gusto alongside an EOR rather than instead of one.

fee_structure.summary: Published Simple-plan pricing starts at $49/month plus $6 per user per month, a per-seat SaaS model rather than the per-employee EOR model its global competitors use.
bullets: Higher tiers add benefits administration and broader HR features. The base plan is payroll-centric.
There is no per-employee EOR fee because there is no EOR service to price.
International contractor payments carry per-transfer costs and FX conversion fees on top of the subscription.
Comparing $6/user against a $599/employee EOR rate is not like-for-like. The two products solve different problems.

gusto.supportSLA: Business-hours Live Chat, Dedicated CSM (Plus+), Knowledge Base
gusto.skip_if: Don't buy Gusto if you need a full-time employee in another country. It can pay contractors. It cannot employ them.

multiplier.positioning: Mid-market EOR priced for APAC and EMEA hiring, starting at $400 per employee per month.
multiplier.text_compliance: Multiplier manages compliance across 150+ countries with automated employment contracts built around local labor laws. They assume employer liability, ensuring statutory benefit contributions, severance policies, and localized tax withholdings meet strict jurisdictional standards.
multiplier.text_global_reach: Multiplier has an exceptionally strong infrastructure footprint across the Asia-Pacific region and emerging markets, providing direct entity support in key tech hubs like India, Singapore, Vietnam, and the UAE alongside broader global coverage.
multiplier.text_pricing_truth: Contractor management starts at $40/month per active contractor. EOR services start at $400/month per employee, positioning Multiplier as one of the more aggressive mid-market EOR price points. Local benefit package add-ons and admin fees should be reviewed country-by-country.
choose_if: Most of the next 18 months of hiring is APAC or EMEA and $400/employee beats a $599 sticker.
You need local contracts generated from templates counsel has already seen.

ip_assignment.summary: Multiplier assumes employer liability and generates employment contracts built around local labor law across 150+ countries, with particular entity depth across Asia-Pacific.
bullets: Employment agreements are localized per jurisdiction rather than templated globally, which is what makes an invention assignment clause enforceable in the first place.
Direct entity support in India, Singapore, Vietnam, and the UAE means the IP chain in those markets avoids a partner intermediary.
APAC jurisdictions differ meaningfully on employee invention compensation, so specific legal review is worthwhile if your R&D headcount sits there.
Confirm the entity model for markets outside Multiplier's core APAC and EMEA strength.

tax_withholding.summary: Multiplier assumes employer liability for statutory benefit contributions, severance policy, and localized tax withholding as part of the EOR service rather than as add-ons.
bullets: Employer contributions and employee withholding are calculated to local standards across 150+ countries.
13th-month salary requirements in markets like Brazil, Italy, and the Philippines form part of statutory employment cost.
Provident fund and social insurance schemes in Multiplier's strongest markets, such as India EPF and Singapore CPF, are administered directly.
Country-by-country administration fees should be reviewed, per Multiplier's own pricing guidance.

statutory_benefits.summary: Multiplier takes on employer liability for statutory benefits and severance, positioned as an aggressive mid-market price point for teams scaling across APAC and EMEA.
bullets: Statutory benefit contributions and severance policies are managed to local jurisdictional standards.
Mandatory PTO floors and public holiday calendars follow the hiring country rather than your HQ policy.
As legal employer, Multiplier carries unlawful termination exposure, which is the key liability shield for a scaling SMB.
Local benefit package add-ons are priced per country. Review these before assuming the $400 rate is all-in.

fee_structure.summary: At $400/month per employee, Multiplier is one of the more aggressive mid-market EOR price points, which makes the add-on lines proportionally more significant to total cost.
bullets: The $400 EOR rate undercuts Deel and Remote at $599 and Oyster HR at $699, but employer taxes still sit on top of all of them.
Local benefit package add-ons and per-country admin fees are Multiplier's own flagged variable costs.
Contractor management is priced separately at $40/month per active contractor.
Verify FX handling and any deposit requirement for your payout corridors, since a low platform fee can be quietly offset by conversion spread.

multiplier.supportSLA: 24/7 Live Chat, Dedicated CSM, Knowledge Base
multiplier.skip_if: Don't buy Multiplier if US multi-state payroll and device identity are the real system of record. This is an EOR, not an IT directory.

payoneer-workforce-management.positioning: Contractor payouts across 190+ countries on Payoneer wallets. No monthly seat. They earn on the transfer.
payoneer-workforce-management.text_compliance: Payoneer Workforce Management automates the contractor-side paperwork most payout tools leave manual: onboarding flows, W-8BEN and W-9 tax form collection, and invoice approval trails are handled in-platform so you keep audit-ready records for every international contractor. It is a contractor management and payments layer rather than an Employer of Record, so it does not assume employer liability, file statutory payroll taxes, or administer localized benefits on your behalf.
payoneer-workforce-management.text_global_reach: Payoneer moves money into 190+ countries from multi-currency wallets, with batch payouts so finance teams can settle an entire contractor roster in one run. Contractors choose how they get paid, via local bank transfer in their own currency, the Payoneer card, or wire, and can hold balances in multiple currencies instead of converting on every invoice.
payoneer-workforce-management.text_pricing_truth: There is no subscription: contractor receiving and management accounts are $0/month, and Payoneer earns on the transfer instead. Cross-border payout fees typically land between 0% and 1% depending on the payout method and corridor, with contractor-to-contractor and wallet transfers at the low end and card or wire withdrawals at the high end. Model your actual currency corridors, since the FX conversion spread, not the headline fee, is where the real cost sits.
choose_if: You pay 5 to 250 contractors, not EOR employees, and you want batch payouts from one wallet.
You need W-8BEN or W-9 collection without a per-contractor SaaS fee.

ip_assignment.summary: Payoneer Workforce Management is a contractor payout and management layer rather than an Employer of Record. It never becomes the employer, so it provides no employer-side IP assignment at all.
bullets: IP assignment sits entirely in the contractor agreement between you and the worker.
Contractors retain more independence than employees by definition, which makes blanket assignment of future inventions harder to enforce in many jurisdictions.
Teams whose core R&D is produced by international contractors carry real IP risk here that an EOR would otherwise absorb.
Onboarding flows and audit-ready records help evidence the relationship, but they are not a substitute for an employment-grade assignment.

tax_withholding.summary: Payoneer automates contractor tax paperwork such as W-8BEN and W-9 collection and invoice approval trails, but does not withhold or file statutory payroll taxes, because it is not the employer.
bullets: W-8BEN and W-9 collection is handled in-platform, keeping US reporting obligations auditable.
No employer contributions, social security, or income tax withholding are performed. The contractor is responsible in their own jurisdiction.
13th-month salary and comparable statutory payroll obligations do not apply to contractor relationships.
This is the trade-off that makes the model cheap: you retain the compliance responsibility an EOR would take on.

statutory_benefits.summary: No statutory benefits are administered. Because Payoneer does not assume employer liability, health cover, pension, PTO, and severance all remain outside its scope entirely.
bullets: Contractors are not entitled to statutory benefits, which is precisely why misclassification is the central risk of this model.
There is no severance calculation, notice-period enforcement, or unlawful termination shield.
A contractor reclassified as an employee by a local authority creates retroactive liability that lands on your company, not on Payoneer.
If you are engaging people who work full-time hours under your direction, an EOR is the correct instrument rather than a payout layer.

fee_structure.summary: There is no subscription. Contractor accounts are $0/month and Payoneer earns on the transfer instead, which moves the entire cost question onto FX spread and payout method.
bullets: Cross-border payout fees typically land between 0% and 1% depending on payout method and corridor.
Wallet-to-wallet transfers sit at the low end, while card and wire withdrawals sit at the high end.
The FX conversion spread rather than the headline fee is where the real cost sits, so model your actual currency corridors.
Against a $499 to $699 per-employee EOR rate this looks dramatically cheaper, but it buys a different service with the compliance risk retained by you.

payoneer-workforce-management.supportSLA: Business-hours Live Chat, Ticketed support, Knowledge Base
payoneer-workforce-management.skip_if: Don't buy Payoneer Workforce Management if you need a local legal employer. There is no EOR here. Payouts are not employment.

remote.positioning: EOR through companies Remote owns in each market. Partner agencies are not in the chain.
remote.text_compliance: Remote owns the legal entity in every market it supports. The employment contract, IP assignment, and misclassification defense sit with Remote, not a third-party agency. If a vendor cannot show the local company name on the contract, you are buying a partner network.
remote.text_global_reach: Remote operates owned-entity EOR infrastructure across 100+ countries while serving global contractor management and payouts in 180+ countries. Their owned-entity model ensures direct control over employee contracts, local payroll, and government tax filings.
remote.text_pricing_truth: Contractor management starts at $29/month per worker, with EOR at $599/month per employee on typical annual commitments ($699 month-to-month). IP protection and owned-entity compliance are included in the base EOR fee.
choose_if: Board and counsel want IP assigned by Remote's own local entity, not a partner agency.
You will pay $599/employee on an annual term and you want that fee to include the entity, not a markup later.

ip_assignment.summary: Remote's central claim is compliance purity: it owns its legal entities in every EOR market, so IP assigns from the worker to a Remote-owned entity and then to you, with no third-party partner agency ever holding the work product.
bullets: IP transfer is included in the base EOR fee rather than sold as a paid add-on.
The owned-entity model removes the sub-licensing chain you inherit with partner-network EORs, where a local agency is the counterparty on the employment agreement.
This matters most for R&D and software teams where the entire asset being created is code, patents, or design work.
Coverage is 100+ owned EOR markets against 180+ contractor countries. Outside the EOR footprint the hire is a contractor, and the same protection does not apply.

tax_withholding.summary: Remote registers as the employer in each owned-entity market and runs localized payroll directly, filing employer contributions, employee income tax, and social security under its own registrations rather than passing them through an intermediary.
bullets: Filings go to the tax authority from Remote itself rather than via a partner, which shortens the correction loop when something is filed wrong.
13th and 14th month obligations in Brazil, Italy, Greece, and the Philippines are accrued monthly so the payment is already funded when it falls due.
Employer contribution rates are surfaced per country before you hire, which is what makes cross-country offer comparisons meaningful.
Contractor payouts at $29/month carry no withholding. That is a separate product with a materially different risk profile.

statutory_benefits.summary: Remote administers the statutory package in each owned market and is explicit that benefits are locally defined rather than globally standardized, which is the honest position for any EOR.
bullets: Statutory health cover, pension, and mandatory leave follow the local floor across the 100+ owned EOR markets.
Notice periods and severance are enforced to local statute, with Remote executing the termination and absorbing the procedural risk.
Unlawful termination exposure sits with Remote's local entity, shielding a small company from foreign labor court proceedings.
Supplemental benefit availability varies by market, so verify what is actually on offer in your specific hiring countries.

fee_structure.summary: Remote positions transparent flat pricing as a differentiator: $599/month per employee on an annual commitment or $699 month-to-month, with IP protection and owned-entity compliance included rather than upsold.
bullets: The $100 per employee per month gap between annual and month-to-month terms is the single biggest lever on Remote's headline cost.
With no partner agency in the chain, there is no third-party markup layered onto the underlying local employment cost.
Employer taxes and statutory contributions still sit on top. The flat rate covers Remote's service, not the cost of employment itself.
Confirm deposit and prefunding requirements for your markets, since these vary and are a cash-flow consideration rather than a line-item fee.

remote.supportSLA: 24/7 Live Chat, Dedicated CSM, Knowledge Base
remote.skip_if: Don't buy Remote if you need same-week coverage in a country they have not built yet. Owned entities move slower than a partner network.

rippling.positioning: US HR, payroll, laptops, and app access on one employee record. Global EOR is a paid module on top.
rippling.text_compliance: Rippling automates compliance across US domestic payroll and global workforce expansions. Its engine automatically enforces local overtime laws, tax registration, mandatory sexual harassment training, and international labor standards based on worker location.
rippling.text_global_reach: Rippling supports global hiring via direct payroll, local entity management, and integrated EOR services. It allows companies to manage US W-2 employees, international EOR staff, and worldwide contractors within a single unified HR cloud.
rippling.text_pricing_truth: The $8/user/month rate buys the core workforce graph only. US payroll, benefits, device management, and global EOR are à la carte modules. An all-in quote for payroll plus IT typically lands at several multiples of the published seat. Comparing $8/user to a $599 EOR rate is not like-for-like.
choose_if: Your system of record is US W-2 plus Google Workspace, laptops, and app access. International EOR is the minority of the roster.
Finance will not sign until payroll, benefits, and devices are separate line items. The $8 seat is not the quote.

ip_assignment.summary: Rippling offers EOR as one module inside a broader workforce operations suite, so IP assignment coverage depends on whether a given worker sits on Rippling's EOR, on your own entity's payroll, or on a contractor agreement.
bullets: For workers on Rippling EOR, the localized employment agreement carries the IP assignment.
For US W-2 staff or workers on your own foreign entity, assignment runs through your contracts. Rippling is the system of record, not the employer.
The unified platform makes it easy to hold all three worker types at once, which also means the IP chain is not uniform across your roster.
Audit which employment vehicle each international hire sits under before assuming consistent protection.

tax_withholding.summary: Rippling's compliance engine enforces tax registration and local labor rules based on worker location, spanning US domestic payroll and international EOR within a single system.
bullets: Automated tax registration and local overtime enforcement adjust to each worker's jurisdiction.
US multi-state payroll is a particular strength, with automatic registration as employees relocate between states.
International withholding depends on whether the worker is on Rippling EOR or on your own foreign entity.
13th-month obligations apply only to EOR workers in the markets that mandate them.

statutory_benefits.summary: Statutory benefit administration follows the module you buy. Rippling EOR carries the employer obligations, while global payroll running on your own entity leaves those obligations with you.
bullets: Rippling EOR workers receive the local statutory package with Rippling's entity as legal employer.
Workers on your own foreign entity remain your legal responsibility. Rippling administers the process but does not assume the liability.
Mandatory training compliance such as state harassment training is automated for US teams.
Confirm which markets Rippling covers directly versus through a partner before relying on the liability shield.

fee_structure.summary: The commonly cited $8/user/month buys the core workforce platform only. Payroll, benefits, IT device management, and global EOR are separately priced modules on top.
bullets: A realistic all-in quote for a team running payroll plus IT typically lands at several multiples of the base rate.
Ask for module-level line items before comparing Rippling against a bundled EOR price.
EOR pricing is quoted separately and is not included in the per-user platform figure.
Device management and app provisioning are genuine cost offsets if they replace separate IT tooling, so count that on the other side of the ledger.

rippling.supportSLA: 24/7 Live Chat, Dedicated CSM, Knowledge Base
rippling.skip_if: Don't buy Rippling if you only hire international contractors. You'll pay for a US HRIS suite you will not touch.

ashby.positioning: ATS, sourcing CRM, and interview scheduling with funnel conversion reporting in the same product. Flat-tier price. No recruiter seats.
ashby.text_compliance: Ashby automates GDPR compliance, candidate data privacy consent workflows, and structured EEOC/OFCCP survey collection. It enforces standardized scorecard criteria across hiring panels to eliminate interviewer bias and ensure auditable hiring records.
ashby.text_global_reach: Ashby supports international recruitment with automated multi-time-zone interview scheduling, multi-currency compensation benchmarking, and localized offer letter workflows across worldwide tech hiring hubs.
ashby.text_pricing_truth: Published Foundations pricing starts at $400/month for companies up to 100 employees, scaling with headcount. There is no free trial; pricing is flat-tier rather than per hiring-manager seat.
choose_if: You need stage-to-offer conversion reporting inside the ATS, not a Looker export.
You want unlimited interviewer seats. Ashby bills by company size, not by hiring manager.
ashby.supportSLA: Dedicated CSM, Ticketed support, Knowledge Base
ashby.skip_if: Don't buy Ashby if you still post two jobs a quarter. Skip it. The analytics package is overkill.

lever.positioning: Outbound sourcing and nurture (LeverTRM) sitting on the same pipeline as inbound applications.
lever.text_compliance: Lever maintains GDPR compliance tools, automated candidate data retention policies, and built-in EEOC survey tracking across all candidate touchpoints and email nurture campaigns.
lever.text_global_reach: Lever supports multi-channel sourcing for remote and international roles: nurture campaigns, candidate rediscovery, and outreach templates. Confirm language support and data residency on the quote. Do not assume a US ATS is ready for EU hiring.
lever.text_pricing_truth: Lever prices on custom annual contracts based on headcount and modules. There is no public self-serve tier; request a quote for Talent Relationship Management and analytics add-ons.
choose_if: Hiring managers will live in the tool. The UI is the reason they leave feedback.
You run nurture sequences for silver medalists and you want that in the ATS, not Mailchimp.
lever.supportSLA: Dedicated CSM, Ticketed support, Knowledge Base
lever.skip_if: Don't buy Lever if you need public pricing and unlimited interviewer seats. Quotes are annual and seat-licensed.

workable.positioning: SMB ATS with one-click posting to 200+ job boards and published monthly prices. Standard starts at $299/month for 1–20 employees.
workable.text_compliance: Workable automates GDPR candidate rights management, EEOC/CCPA compliance collection, and background check integrations across 100+ countries with built-in audit trails.
workable.text_global_reach: Workable posts jobs to 200+ global job boards in a single click and offers built-in AI sourcing (AI Recruiter) that searches a database of 400+ million global candidate profiles.
workable.text_pricing_truth: Workable Standard starts at $299/month for teams of 1–20 employees (headcount-banded). Premier and Enterprise tiers and paid add-ons (texting, video, assessments) can raise total cost well above the Standard floor.
choose_if: You want jobs on Indeed, LinkedIn, and local boards without a sourcer buying slots by hand.
You will not sit through a six-week enterprise RFP for a 15-person hiring team.
workable.supportSLA: Live Chat, Dedicated CSM (Premier+), Knowledge Base
workable.skip_if: Don't buy Workable if OFCCP reporting and SSO are the RFP. That packaging lives on Premier and Enterprise, not Standard.

breezy-hr.positioning: Kanban hiring pipeline with built-in video screening. Paid plans commonly start near $189/month. There is a free tier.
breezy-hr.text_compliance: Breezy HR handles GDPR consent prompts, candidate data deletion requests, and automated EEOC survey collection with minimal administrative setup.
breezy-hr.text_global_reach: Breezy HR distributes job openings to major international job boards including Indeed, LinkedIn, and ZipRecruiter, supporting remote team recruiting workflows.
breezy-hr.text_pricing_truth: Breezy HR offers a free tier for limited hiring volume, with paid plans commonly starting around $189/month for unlimited jobs and candidates. Confirm current free-tier limits before modeling SMB rollout cost.
choose_if: Your team will drag cards on a board. If they will not, skip every ATS.
You need async video screens and self-serve scheduling without buying a second tool.
breezy-hr.supportSLA: Live Chat (paid plans), Email support, Knowledge Base
breezy-hr.skip_if: Don't buy Breezy HR if legal needs an OFCCP file. This is an SMB pipeline, not a federal-contractor audit system.

jazzhr.positioning: SMB ATS starting near $75/month with unlimited interviewer seats and syndication to Indeed, ZipRecruiter, and Google for Jobs.
jazzhr.text_compliance: JazzHR ensures OFCCP and EEOC compliance with built-in reporting tools, automated candidate survey tracking, and secure document storage for audit preparation.
jazzhr.text_global_reach: JazzHR focuses primarily on US domestic and North American SMB hiring, syndicating openings across dozens of regional and national job boards with custom career page widgets.
jazzhr.text_pricing_truth: Published plans start around $75/month for entry-level job limits, scaling upward for unlimited postings. Unlimited user seats keep interviewer collaboration costs predictable for SMBs.
choose_if: Budget is under $100/month and every hiring manager needs a login.
You want jobs on Indeed and ZipRecruiter without a second job-board contract.
jazzhr.supportSLA: Email support, Ticketed SLA, Knowledge Base
jazzhr.skip_if: Don't buy JazzHR if you need a sourcing CRM and structured scorecards that block advancing a candidate. This is tracking, not recruiting ops.

recruitee.positioning: European hiring platform with a multi-language careers site and GDPR as a default, not an add-on.
recruitee.text_compliance: Recruitee provides enterprise-grade GDPR compliance automation, strict candidate consent timers, and localized data residency in European data centers.
recruitee.text_global_reach: Recruitee excels for European and multi-national teams with multi-language careers page localization, localized job board syndication, and multi-currency tracking.
recruitee.text_pricing_truth: Pricing starts at $199/month on the Launch tier (job-slot based) with unlimited team members, scaling to Scale and custom enterprise quotes for high-volume hiring.
choose_if: You hire in the EU and candidate consent has to survive a DPA review.
You need a branded careers site in more than one language without a web team.
recruitee.supportSLA: Live Chat, Dedicated CSM (Scale+), Knowledge Base
recruitee.skip_if: Don't buy Recruitee if the only office is US and you wanted OFCCP reporting. Buy a US-first ATS.

bamboohr-ats.name: BambooHR
bamboohr-ats.positioning: The hiring module inside BambooHR. Candidate records become employee files. There is no standalone ATS price list.
bamboohr-ats.text_compliance: BambooHR connects directly with the core HRIS database to ensure EEOC compliance, secure e-signatures, and seamless candidate-to-employee onboarding records.
bamboohr-ats.text_global_reach: BambooHR supports international applicant tracking for organizations expanding across multiple country locations using the primary BambooHR platform.
bamboohr-ats.text_pricing_truth: BambooHR ATS capabilities are sold as part of custom-quoted Advantage/Pro HRIS packages rather than a standalone public price list. Expect implementation and per-employee HRIS fees to dominate total cost versus a point ATS.
choose_if: BambooHR is already the HRIS, or it will be. Hired candidates should become employees without a CSV.
Recruiting approvals happen in the same mobile app as time off.
bamboohr-ats.supportSLA: Phone + Live Chat, Dedicated CSM (Pro), Knowledge Base
bamboohr-ats.skip_if: Don't buy BambooHR ATS if you do not run BambooHR. You will pay for an HRIS to get a pipeline.

performyard.positioning: Review cycles, goals, and 360 feedback you can configure without a six-month implementation. About $5/user/month.
performyard.text_compliance: PerformYard provides configurable review templates, role-based permissions, and retained review history suitable for HR audit trails, with standard SOC 2 and GDPR-oriented data practices for employee performance records.
performyard.text_global_reach: PerformYard works well for US and mid-market multi-location employers that need consistent review cycles across departments, with Slack integrations for feedback reminders rather than deep multi-language localization.
performyard.text_pricing_truth: Plans typically start at $5/user/month depending on modules and review-cycle complexity. There is no published free trial. Buyers should expect a demo-led sales motion. Implementation is lighter than enterprise suites; advanced compensation options may be quoted separately.
choose_if: You are replacing Google Docs reviews and you need templates live this quarter.
You want 1:1s and 360s without paying Lattice or Culture Amp enterprise rates.
performyard.supportSLA: Dedicated CSM, Ticketed SLA, Knowledge Base
performyard.skip_if: Don't buy PerformYard if compensation calibration is the buying reason. That module is quoted later, and Lattice still owns that fight.

lattice.positioning: Reviews, OKRs, engagement, and compensation calibration for companies that actually run a talent cycle.
lattice.text_compliance: Lattice supports enterprise access controls, talent-review confidentiality, compensation-band governance, and audit-friendly performance history designed for regulated and large-employer review processes.
lattice.text_global_reach: Lattice serves global and multi-entity employers with multi-language support, HRIS integrations, and workflows for distributed talent calibration across regions and business units.
lattice.text_pricing_truth: Performance modules commonly start around $10/user/month, with Goals & OKRs from $8/user/month and Engagement/Compensation sold as add-ons. Contracts are demo-led with a minimum annual spend. Model total seat cost across modules before comparing to lighter tools.
choose_if: Pay decisions have to sit on the same calibration table as performance ratings.
People partners run a formal cycle and need analytics, not a spreadsheet export.
lattice.supportSLA: Dedicated CSM, Enterprise SLA, Knowledge Base
lattice.skip_if: Don't buy Lattice if you wanted weekly 1:1s and nothing else. You will fund engagement and compensation modules you will not turn on.

culture-amp.positioning: Engagement surveys and external benchmarks first. Performance and development sit on that data.
culture-amp.text_compliance: Culture Amp provides enterprise-grade survey anonymity controls, GDPR-aligned data handling, and role-based access for sensitive engagement and performance insights used in People Ops decision-making.
culture-amp.text_global_reach: Culture Amp supports large global workforces with multi-language surveys, regional benchmarks, and distributed action-planning workflows for international People teams.
culture-amp.text_pricing_truth: Culture Amp uses custom quotes for Engage/Perform/Develop bundles based on headcount and module mix. Expect a demo-led enterprise sales motion rather than self-serve published pricing.
choose_if: The buying reason is survey science and benchmarks, not a review form.
People Ops will act on org-wide results, not a three-question pulse in Slack.
culture-amp.supportSLA: Dedicated CSM, Enterprise SLA, Knowledge Base
culture-amp.skip_if: Don't buy Culture Amp if you only needed a review cycle. You will sit through an enterprise survey rollout to get a performance module.

oyster-hr.name: Oyster HR
oyster-hr.positioning: Global employment for mid-market remote companies. Contractor product at $29/month after a 30-day trial. EOR listed at $699/employee.
oyster-hr.text_compliance: Oyster HR automates local employment agreements and statutory compliance in 180+ countries. They handle misclassification safeguards, localized IP assignments, and statutory benefit filings through a mix of owned infrastructure and local HR partners.
oyster-hr.text_global_reach: Oyster lists 180+ countries with local-currency payouts and local benefits admin. Some markets run through partner entities, not Oyster-owned companies. Get the owned-versus-partner list for the two countries you will hire next.
oyster-hr.text_pricing_truth: Contractor management starts at $29/month after a 30-day free trial, with EOR listed at $699/month per employee on the public pricing page (volume/annual seat discounts may apply). Watch FX spreads and any required salary deposits when modeling total cost of ownership.
choose_if: You will try contractors for 30 days before converting anyone to EOR.
You need a country cost calculator before the offer letter, not after.

ip_assignment.summary: Oyster HR automates localized IP assignment as part of its employment agreements, delivered through a mix of owned infrastructure and local HR partners across 180+ countries.
bullets: Assignment clauses are localized per country rather than applied as a single global template.
Because coverage blends owned entities and local partners, the assignment chain differs by market. Ask Oyster HR which model applies to your hiring countries.
Misclassification safeguards reinforce the assignment, since a contractor reclassified as an employee can undermine the original IP transfer.
The platform is oriented toward distributed design and engineering teams, which is where the strength of a clean IP chain matters most.

tax_withholding.summary: Oyster HR handles statutory benefit filings and localized tax withholding across its 180+ country footprint, paying workers in their local currency by default.
bullets: Employer contributions and employee withholding are calculated at local rates and filed on the local schedule.
13th-month obligations in markets such as Brazil, Italy, and the Philippines are treated as part of statutory employment cost.
Local currency payout shifts FX exposure onto the platform's conversion rate rather than onto the employee.
Given the mixed owned and partner model, confirm which entity carries the filing obligation in each of your markets.

statutory_benefits.summary: Oyster HR administers localized benefits tailored to distributed teams, with statutory filings handled through owned infrastructure or local HR partners depending on the market.
bullets: Statutory health cover, pension, and mandatory leave follow each country's legal floor.
Notice periods and severance are enforced to local statute, with Oyster HR as the employing party in EOR markets.
Termination liability shielding is the core EOR benefit for an SMB hiring its first employee in a new country.
Benefits depth can differ between owned-entity and partner markets, so verify coverage for your specific countries.

fee_structure.summary: Oyster HR publishes $699/month per employee for EOR and $29/month for contractors after a 30-day trial, and its own guidance points to FX spreads and salary deposits as the lines that move total cost.
bullets: At $699 the published EOR rate sits above Deel and Remote's $599 annual-commitment pricing, though volume and annual discounts may apply.
FX spread on local-currency payouts is a real cost that never appears in the per-employee rate.
Required salary deposits are a working-capital commitment rather than a fee. Model the cash impact separately.
The 30-day free trial applies to contractor management, not to EOR hiring.

oyster-hr.supportSLA: 24/7 Live Chat, Dedicated CSM, Knowledge Base
oyster-hr.skip_if: Don't buy Oyster HR if the first hire is tomorrow and the country sits on a partner entity. Ask who the legal employer is before you sign.

papaya-global.positioning: Multi-country payroll reporting for finance teams running owned entities and EOR side by side. EOR from $650/employee.
papaya-global.text_compliance: Papaya Global uses AI-driven compliance engine checks paired with local in-country experts across 160+ jurisdictions. They oversee mandatory tax filings, worker classification risks, and legal contract amendments for complex corporate structures.
papaya-global.text_global_reach: Operating in over 160 countries, Papaya Global specializes in unifying fragmented international payroll networks. They allow multinational enterprises to manage localized EOR workers, direct payroll entities, and global contractors from a single business intelligence console.
papaya-global.text_pricing_truth: Contractor management and payments are $25–$30/month per contractor. Full-Service EOR starts at $650/month per employee, with Premium EOR at $770/month. Payroll-only / direct-entity global payroll is $12–$25/month per employee. Implementation fees, platform minimums, and country complexity can raise the all-in rate; complex benefit administration and deposits are quoted separately.
choose_if: Finance needs one payroll file across owned subsidiaries and EOR workers.
You already have 20+ countries and an ERP. Implementation overhead is the point.

ip_assignment.summary: Papaya Global serves multinationals running a hybrid of owned foreign subsidiaries alongside EOR workers, so IP assignment depends on which employment vehicle each worker sits under. That distinction matters more here than with single-model providers.
bullets: Workers hired through your own subsidiary assign IP directly to that entity, while EOR workers assign through Papaya Global's in-country arrangement.
Coverage across 160+ jurisdictions uses a mix of owned infrastructure and local partners. Ask which model applies in each market you hire in.
Where a local partner is the employing entity, the IP chain includes a sub-licensing step. Request the specific assignment wording for those markets.
Legal contract amendments are handled by Papaya Global's in-country experts, which is the practical route to strengthening a weak assignment clause.

tax_withholding.summary: Payroll intelligence is Papaya Global's core product. It consolidates localized withholding, employer contributions, and statutory filings across many countries into a single reporting console built for enterprise finance teams.
bullets: The differentiator is consolidated multi-country payroll reporting rather than the mechanics of withholding, which every EOR performs.
Mandatory 13th and 14th month payments are handled as part of localized payroll in the markets that require them.
The BI layer is what lets a CFO compare employer tax burden across countries side by side, which is usually the real reason enterprises choose this over a cheaper EOR.
Complex or unusual jurisdictions may route through local partners, so confirm who carries filing responsibility per market.

statutory_benefits.summary: Papaya Global administers statutory benefits across its jurisdiction network and explicitly flags complex benefit administration as an area that carries add-on cost, which is worth scoping during the quote rather than after signature.
bullets: Statutory health, pension, and leave entitlements are administered locally across 160+ jurisdictions.
Papaya Global's own pricing guidance calls out add-on costs for complex benefit administration.
Severance and notice-period enforcement follow local statute, with legal amendments handled by in-country experts.
For enterprises operating in 20+ countries, consolidated benefit reporting is often worth more than a per-employee rate difference.

fee_structure.summary: Papaya Global publishes four 2026 tiers: Full-Service EOR from $650/month per employee, Premium EOR at $770/month, contractor management at $25–$30/month, and payroll-only / direct-entity processing at $12–$25/month per employee. Deposits and add-ons still move the all-in number.
bullets: Full-Service EOR starts at $650/employee/month. Premium EOR is $770/employee/month.
Contractor management and payments are $25–$30/contractor/month. Payroll-only / direct-entity global payroll is $12–$25/employee/month.
Papaya Global's guidance explicitly calls out security deposits, commonly framed as one to two months of salary held upfront.
Complex benefit administration is an add-on rather than bundled into the base rate. Do not blend EOR, contractor, and payroll-only fees when building a TCO comparison.

papaya-global.supportSLA: 24/7 Dedicated CSM, White-glove implementation, Knowledge Base
papaya-global.name: Papaya Global
papaya-global.skip_if: Don't buy Papaya Global if you have 40 people and one country. You will fund an enterprise payroll rollout you cannot staff.
